question: Is our support ticket data current enough to act on today?

input.purpose: Check freshness of Zendesk ticket data: latest sync time, latest ticket create/update timestamps, and row counts.
input.sql: SELECT 'zendesk.ticket' AS tbl, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS last_synced, MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at, MAX(created_at) AS max_created_at, COUNT(*) AS row_count, SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_deleted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS deleted_rows FROM zendesk.ticket

input.purpose: Check sync freshness for related Zendesk tables (ticket_tag, organization) to confirm the whole Zendesk feed is current.
input.sql: SELECT 'zendesk.ticket_tag' AS tbl, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS last_synced, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM zendesk.ticket_tag UNION ALL SELECT 'zendesk.organization', MAX(_fivetran_synced), COUNT(*) FROM zendesk.organization

input.purpose: Compare sync timestamps across all four source systems to see whether the future-dated Zendesk sync is an isolated anomaly or a feed-wide clock issue.
input.sql:
SELECT 'zendesk.ticket' AS tbl, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS last_synced, MIN(_fivetran_synced) AS first_synced FROM zendesk.ticket
UNION ALL SELECT 'carrier_pg.shipment', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM carrier_pg.shipment
UNION ALL SELECT 'carrier_pg.shipment_event', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM carrier_pg.shipment_event
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.account
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.opportunity', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.opportunity
UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.likp', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM sap_s4.likp
UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.vbak', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM sap_s4.vbak

input.purpose: Look at the distribution of Zendesk ticket sync timestamps and recent ticket activity to see whether the sync times are plausible.
input.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', _fivetran_synced) AS sync_day, COUNT(*) AS tickets_synced FROM zendesk.ticket GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 20

input.purpose: Check daily Zendesk ticket creation volume over the last 6 weeks to see whether tickets stop after Nov 3 (a feed gap) or volume is just low.
input.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at) AS created_day, COUNT(*) AS tickets_created FROM zendesk.ticket WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-09-20' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC

input.purpose: Check latest activity in the carrier shipment table to see whether operational data also stops around Nov 3, which would point to a source-side gap rather than a Zendesk-only issue.
input.sql: SELECT MAX(updated_at) AS max_shipment_updated, MAX(created_at) AS max_shipment_created, MAX(event_at) AS max_event_at FROM (SELECT s.updated_at, s.created_at, NULL::timestamptz AS event_at FROM carrier_pg.shipment s UNION ALL SELECT NULL, NULL, e.event_at FROM carrier_pg.shipment_event e) x

answer.answer_summary: No, the Zendesk support ticket data is not current enough to act on today. The newest ticket was created on 3 November 2026 (last update 18:00 UTC), and there are no tickets from 4 to 6 November, even though the carrier system has activity through 6 November and ticket volume usually runs about 7 a day. The Zendesk sync timestamps (9 November) are also later than the as-of date, so the feed's timing is unreliable until it is re-extracted and checked.

metrics_used.name: Latest ticket activity
metrics_used.definition: Maximum created_at and updated_at in zendesk.ticket, compared with the 6 Nov 2026 as-of date.

metrics_used.name: Daily ticket creation volume
metrics_used.definition: Count of zendesk.ticket rows by created_at day, 20 Sep to 3 Nov 2026; baseline roughly 7 tickets per day.

metrics_used.name: Sync recency
metrics_used.definition: MAX(_fivetran_synced) per source table, compared with the as-of date.

lineage: zendesk.ticket -> data freshness check (max created_at, updated_at, _fivetran_synced)
zendesk.ticket_tag and zendesk.organization -> sync recency check
carrier_pg.shipment and carrier_pg.shipment_event -> cross-system activity comparison
assumptions: The as-of date of 6 November 2026 is correct and is the reference point for 'today'.
The gap in ticket creation (4 to 6 November) is real and not a legitimate lull in support demand; the baseline of about 7 tickets a day is the expected rate.
Ticket updated_at values are reliable for detecting the last change.
caveats: Every Zendesk ticket has the same _fivetran_synced value (one batch, 9 Nov 19:47 UTC). That looks like a full reload, and the timestamp is after the as-of date, so the sync clock or the as-of date may be wrong.
The other source systems also have sync timestamps dated 11 Nov, after the as-of date, so the clock issue may be feed-wide.
About 20 tickets may be missing for 4 to 6 November (roughly 3 days at about 7 a day). This is an estimate, not a confirmed count.
The 3 November count is probably partial, since the latest ticket was created at 16:33 UTC.
Before acting, confirm with the Zendesk integration owner that the extract is complete through 6 November and that the sync clock is correct.

explanation.title: Counted cancelled deliveries
explanation.detail: The SAP tables keep 310 cancelled deliveries as soft-deleted rows (_fivetran_deleted = true). This query never filters them out, so cancelled deliveries count as late.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.likp', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM sap_s4.likp

explanation.title: Missed a customer split across two CRM accounts
explanation.detail: Halbrook Fluid Systems has a look-alike duplicate account ("… GmbH") with no SAP number. Two of its open shipping tickets sit on the duplicate, so the customer looked healthy.

explanation.title: Read every history row of the account tier
explanation.detail: salesforce.account keeps one row per version of each account (history mode). Without filtering to _fivetran_active, accounts that changed tier appear twice, and Quenmere Paper Mills GmbH still looks Strategic.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MIN(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.account
